answer: Admission is priced in human presence: a verifier called NotarySeal accepts only an affidavit signed before a commissioned notary, and rejects any commission ID that certified more than twenty seats a month. The penalty trigger is a commission audit, where a notary whose signers turn out to be one operator loses the batch, bonds burned and seal revoked. At fifteen dollars a signature plus half an hour, ten thousand fakes cost one hundred fifty thousand dollars and five thousand hours, so no canyon of proxies bridges it, no forge of copied stamps survives, and a lotus of cheap seats wilts.
